title: Zoox purpose-built robotaxis get first-ever nod from NHTSA for paid rides
summary: No steering wheel, no pedals, no problem: Zoox will start charging customers for rides in Las Vegas next month, following approval by local regulators.

title: Seattle peels back environmental review appeals in effort to ramp up housing development
summary: The reform eliminates an administrative step that has held up new zoning and housing planning efforts, advocates say.

title: SNAP cuts could shift new costs onto cities, mayors say
summary: Emergency services could be impacted, and the reduced federal food assistance and higher administrative costs will ripple through local economies, city leaders warn.

title: $610M available for FTA bus grants
summary: This round could close out five years of Federal Transit Administration bus investments from the 2021 bipartisan infrastructure law, with future funding uncertain.

title: These cities’ short-term rental income spiked the most from the World Cup
summary: A 60% average surge in short-term rental income was not evenly distributed among host cities, an analysis found — largely due to local regulations.

title: Boston’s $10B coastal resilience infrastructure plan wins access to billions in federal funding
summary: The city qualifies for a 65% federal cost share following a U.S. Army Corps feasibility study, paving the way for more than 20 flood-protection projects expected to prevent $41 billion in damages.

title: Trump reveals plans for $22.5B Dulles airport overhaul
summary: Municipal bonds and public-private partnership opportunities would finance Trump’s plan to modernize Washington Dulles International Airport.

title: AI adoption by local governments outpaces public trust: survey
summary: Transparency about AI use and quality of digital infrastructure were among the issues where resident perceptions were less favorable, the survey found.

title: Washington Union Station renovation seeks private investment
summary: The U.S. Department of Transportation will invest $24 million to develop a public-private partnership, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said.

title: Accessible pedestrian signal rollout in Chicago ahead of targets, but technical gaps persist: report
summary: Improvements are needed to ensure blind and low-vision pedestrians can safely use the system, inspectors say, but the city has exceeded its court-ordered installation requirement.
